en: The perfectly symmetrical cone of Mayon Volcano in Albay is clearly visible from Legazpi City due to its steep, smooth slopes.
Inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, you can ride a boat through a dark cave where an underground river flows.
Philippine tarsiers in Bohol have enormous eyes that are larger than their brains, allowing them to clearly see insects in the dark.
Carved into the Ifugao mountains, the Banaue Rice Terraces look like giant green staircases following the natural contours of the hills.
The grass covering the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turns brown during the dry season, making the mounds look like giant chocolates.
Whale sharks, locally called butanding, gather in Donsol, Sorsogon, where you can observe them filter-feeding on plankton near the ocean surface.
From the Tagaytay ridge, you can clearly observe Taal Volcano sitting as a small island in the middle of Taal Lake.
Inside Sagada's Sumaguing Cave, you can observe large stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites rising from the cave floor.
Mangrove trees in coastal areas like Pambujan have visible arching roots that rise above the muddy water to help the plants breathe.
You can observe thousands of synchronous fireflies lighting up at the exact same time along the trees bordering the Loboc River.
During the amihan season, you can observe cool northeast winds bringing clear skies and dry weather across most of the Philippines.
Snorkelers at Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park can observe vibrant coral walls that drop straight down into the deep blue ocean water.
